rationale: C07, C17, and C16 are the strongest formal analogues because each amends detailed regulations through numbered provisions using formulas such as “is amended to read as follows,” revocation, insertion, redesignation, and substitution. But these are routine mechanisms for amendatory executive orders. None concerns the Foreign Service fee tariff, reproduces the child’s distinctive combination of fee revisions and Immigration and Nationality Act conforming changes, or shares a sufficiently distinctive sequence of provisions to support material template reuse.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Paragraphs (a) and (b) of section V-15 ... are amended to read as follows
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C07: Paragraph (a) of § 1622.14 ... is amended to read as follows
shared_material.explanation: The formula and regulation-amending structure match, but the language is standard amendatory drafting and the substantive schemes are unrelated.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The following item is included immediately below ...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C16: By inserting immediately following § 1604.1 ... the following new section
shared_material.explanation: Both use targeted insertion instructions, but this is generic codified-regulation editing rather than distinctive shared machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Except as otherwise provided herein, this order shall become effective ...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C17: This order shall become effective on May 27, 1953.
shared_material.explanation: Both contain effective-date clauses, which are routine and provide no meaningful evidence of template dependence.
